statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-27820 (GHSA-g857-hhfv-j68w): in the Ruby zlib gem 3.2.2 and earlier (and before 3.1.2 and 3.0.1 on the older lines), Zlib::GzipReader#ungetc prepends bytes in zstream_buffer_ungets without first making sure the output buffer has room, so the memmove that shifts the existing data can overflow it. It is fixed in zlib 3.2.3 by https://github.com/ruby/zlib/commit/608d2be66fcbcb759cbe26c82e95f4381b8dd140, which always expands the buffer before the move: https://github.com/ruby/zlib/security/advisories/GHSA-g857-hhfv-j68w, https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/03/05/buffer-overflow-zlib-cve-2026-27820. Ruby 3.4.8 bundles zlib 3.2.1 and Ruby 3.4.9 bundles zlib 3.2.3: at the v3_4_8 tag ext/zlib/zlib.c defines RUBY_ZLIB_VERSION 3.2.1 and still expands the buffer only when its capacity check fails, and at the v3_4_9 tag it defines 3.2.3 and always expands it. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI ruby-3.4 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 3.4.8-r0, 3.4.8-r1, 3.4.9-r1, 3.4.9-r2, 3.4.10-r2, 3.4.10-r3, 3.4.11-r3, 3.4.12-r3, 3.4.13-r3 and 3.4.13-r4, each for x86_64 and aarch64. We downloaded every package built from the ruby-3.4 source in that repository for both architectures, 432 package files, each checked against its repository index checksum, and read their contents. The Zlib::GzipReader code is in one ELF file per build, the zlib.so extension in ruby-3.4-libs; no other ELF file in these packages contains the GzipReader class name, and none of them contains a static archive, a PE file or a Mach-O file. The zlib default gem specification and the version string compiled into zlib.so are 3.2.1 in 3.4.8-r0 and 3.4.8-r1, and 3.2.3 in 3.4.9-r1 and every later build, and both architectures agree for every build. The range ends at 3.4.9-r1, the first build that ships zlib 3.2.3.
